memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When Pharaoh heard of this, he tried to kill Moses, but Moses fled from Pharaoh and went to live in Midian, where he sat down by a well." - Exodus 2:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In a single verse, Moses loses everything. Prince of Egypt one day, fugitive the next. He runs into the desert and sits down by a well — alone, with no plan, no home, and no future.

Forty years of privilege ended in an afternoon. Humanly speaking, this was the failure that finished him.

God saw it differently. The palace had given Moses education and confidence. The wilderness would give him something he needed far more: humility, patience, and forty years of learning to shepherd stubborn creatures across dry land. He could not have led Israel without both.

If you are sitting by a well right now — a career that collapsed, a plan that failed, a season where you have been set aside — do not assume God has finished with you. Some of God's most important training happens in places that feel like exile.

The desert is not the end of the story. It is where God prepares deliverers.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What failure am I treating as final?
2. What might God be teaching me in this quiet season that success could never teach?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when my plans collapse, help me to trust that You are still preparing me. Teach me what I could not learn any other way. Amen.
